Root cause: _poll returns None for every not-ready state, so the route cannot tell PENDING (lost or expired) from STARTED (running; worker.py:30 sets task_track_started=True and explain_task.py:26 sets STARTED). Once the design is older than STALE_AFTER_S (300 s, measured from design.updated_at, which never moves), every poll while the task is running calls queue_explanation again with the same task id. The solo-pool worker runs these copies one after another, 45-90 s each; each copy sets STARTED again, so every poll during it queues one more. The queue never drains, and the poll that would see SUCCESS and save the text rarely lands in the short gap between copies. It starts whenever the first poll comes after 300 s (old design reopened, or a worker backlog over 5 min). Smallest fix: make _poll return the Celery state; re-queue only when the state is PENDING (never STARTED/RETRY), and at most once per design version, recorded durably (e.g. save_output kind 'explanation_requeued' checked before re-queueing). Test: mock AsyncResult as STARTED with design age 600 s, poll 5 times, assert apply_async called 0 times; as PENDING, assert called exactly once over 5 polls.

Wrong pinout is a FALSE PASS on our own boards (found by the master via the swapped_pins calibration case). IV.2 returns "no part could be compared" for the whole board because part_pinouts.lookup() finds no KiCad symbol for our MPN 2N2222A (KiCad has PN2222A etc.), and the gate still emits (verify_board ok=True, emit=True). Two defects: (1) MPN-to-symbol lookup gap; (2) an uncompared pinout must not let the gate emit fab files (plan decision 9: unknown pinout blocks export). Caution: name bridging is itself the SOT-23/TO-92 trap - PN2222A is E-B-C but onsemi P2N2222A (TO-92) is C-B-E. Bridge only by orderable part number + package, or a page-cited datasheet record (T2); otherwise refuse.

Reproduced the lookup half: part_pinouts.lookup('2N2222A','TO-92') -> "no KiCad symbol is named for '2N2222A'". The KiCad 10 index has PN2222A, MMBT2222A, PMBT2222A, PZT2222A, FFB2222A, but no 2N2222A. Exact match misses, and the prefix rule (:313) needs want.startswith(base), which '2N2222A' vs 'PN2222A' fails. That is correct behaviour: name bridging would be the TO-92 trap. Defect 1 is a data gap, not a matcher bug. Defect 2 is the real one: _check_part_pinouts files the part under 'unchecked' and returns IV.2 status 'unknown' ('no part could be compared') plus IV.2b 'unknown'. Report.gate (:119-125) refuses only on failed() findings, so unknown never blocks; gate().emit stays True and ok=True. compile_board.py:237 then returns verified:true. Plan decision 9 (implementation plan :145) says an unknown pinout blocks export; it is not implemented. Smallest fix: (a) Report.gate refuses emit when IV.2b lists any non-symmetric part (unknown pinout = REFUSED, or at most 'EMITTED WITH RESIDUALS' with no fab files), with a test from the swapped_pins calibration case; (b) for the lookup gap, add an explicit, page-cited override table keyed on (orderable MPN, package) -> pin map (e.g. 2N2222A TO-92 E-B-C per the maker's datasheet, cited), consulted before the KiCad index, never a name alias. Two causes. (1) Build id drift: the sketch header prints 'Simulation validated: {{ ir.simulation_passed or pending }}'. The build hash (project.py:40-44) is the SHA-256 of the file contents, so it covers that line. generate returns the hash with simulation_passed=None ('pending', build 12fc1a04...). When the simulation finishes, simulate.py:100 writes simulation_passed=True into the stored IR. The next GET /firmware computes a new hash (43efdcdb..., the final source says 'Simulation validated: True'), finds no build row, and dispatches a second compile; the first build is orphaned. Each simulation result therefore costs a full PlatformIO build and resets 'compiling', which is most of the ~10 min. (2) '0 workers': /health/worker (main.py:121) uses celery control.ping(timeout=2). The local benchmark worker runs the solo pool (alpha/status.md; docker-compose.yml:34 uses prefork --concurrency=2, which would answer), and a solo worker cannot answer a ping while it is executing a task (here a compile), so a busy worker reads as 'none'. Smallest fix: (1) remove simulation state (and any other mutable IR field) from the firmware templates, or exclude it from the hash, so the build key depends only on what is compiled; test: same IR with simulation_passed None/True gives the same project hash. (2) Report 'busy or none' when ping is empty but a task is active (e.g. inspect via a Redis heartbeat key the task sets), or run the worker with a prefork/threads pool of >= 2.

note: Placement is greedy bounding-box wirelength: each part goes where the sum, over its pads, of the distance to the NEAREST placed pad on the same net is smallest (:127). For a 100 nF cap on VCC_5V/GND, the nearest VCC_5V pad can be R1 or U2 rather than U1 pin 7/20, so the cap lands next to whatever rail pad is closest, 5.07 mm from AVCC and 10.98 mm from VCC. The placer does not know a cap is a decoupling cap or which IC power pin it serves, and verify.py has no decoupling check, so nothing flags it. Also the IR gives one cap for two supply pins (VCC 7, AVCC 20), so <= 6 mm to each cannot be met by one cap on a DIP-28 (the pins are ~16 mm apart). Smallest fix: (1) mark decoupling caps in the netlist (role 'decoupling', target ref + pin), place each right after its IC with cost = distance to its target pin (hard limit 6 mm); (2) a verify.py rule V.decoupling (rung 'rule check', citing the Microchip 6 mm guidance) that fails > 6 mm.
